Hey Product Hunt!

I'm Natalie, an engineer who got tired of text-to-CAD.  
  
They all make up geometry. I wanted the opposite: trace what's really there, and use AI only where it helps.  
  
Upload a photo, sketch, scan or PDF and get an editable DXF and SVG you can cut, mill or print. Converting is free, so try as many as you like.  
  
I set out to build scan-to-CAD, but 2D worked first, so I'm launching that. Bevell Sketchpad is in beta for editing results, and 3D is next.  
  
Please break it. That's how Bevell improves.  
  
Keep building,  
Natalie

results.title: CAD Automation & CAD Software for Engineering Productivity
results.content:
CAD automation helps engineering teams to work faster, more accurately, and streamline their workflows instead of spending time on repetitive tasks, which allows them to concentrate on innovation. As a matter of fact, research indicates that engineers waste as much as 40 percent of their time in redundant CAD activities, and so automation opens up a huge potential.

This blog discusses the benefits of CAD automation in improving the efficiency of the engineers and why it is an indispensable practice in the contemporary business environment.

 ## What is CAD Automation and Why It Matters in Modern Engineering

  CAD automation is the application of scripts, macros, parametric modeling and rule-based systems to automate the repetitive design and documentation operations in CAD software. [...] CAD automation minimizes these risks by:

  + The use of pre-established rules and constraints of design.
  + Conducting automated verification tests.
  + Standardization of outputs in projects.
  + The result is very uniform and accurate designs.

  Automation also facilitates the fact that all the designs are in the same line and therefore, there are not discrepancies between teams and projects.

  The productivity is seriously affected:

  + Fewer revisions
  + Reduced rework
  + Improved product quality

  This high degree of accuracy is directly translated into cost-saving and expedited approvals in the industries where it is essential such as in automotive, aerospace, and manufacturing industries.
 ## Accelerating Design Iterations and Time-to-Market [...] Furthermore, automation becomes a part of larger engineering systems such as PLM (Product Lifecycle Management) and the transitions between design and manufacturing are less problematic.
 ## Eliminating Repetitive Tasks to Save Engineering Time

  Repetitive work, whether it is making similar parts, revising drawings, or even reusing design rules is one of the largest productivity killers in engineering.

  The solution of CAD automation is:

  + Automation of routine operations using macros and scripts.
  + Developing parameteric templates of reusable designs.
  + Creation of automatic dimensions and annotations.

  This implies that engineers do not have to begin afresh with each design iteration.

results.title: CAD Software Comparison: How to Evaluate Alternatives and Choose the Right Tool
results.content:
Choosing the right CAD toolset is a high-impact decision that affects how quickly teams can design, collaborate, and deliver products to market. But with so many CAD alternatives, each promising cloud design workflows, deep functionality, automation, and platform scalability, it’s difficult to determine which solution best supports your team’s long-term success. This guide will break down how major CAD players stack up, and provide a practical checklist to help businesses choose a CAD software that scales with their design and engineering teams.

## Comparing CAD Software for Product Development [...] ## Comparing CAD Software for Product Development

Businesses don’t evaluate CAD alternatives for just one reason. Sometimes it’s about adopting more modern design workflows, other times it’s about removing friction that limits team productivity. Rising licensing and hardware costs, tool capability limitations, or software that can’t support fast-paced collaboration and automation all tend to lead back to the same three drivers: cost, power, and innovation. Depending on which of these three camps you fall into, the “best” alternative changes.

Let’s look at how the biggest players in the market, Onshape, Fusion, CATIA, Creo, NX, Inventor, and SOLIDWORKS, stack up against these buyer motivations.

ALL-ROUNDER

## Onshape

PTC's cloud-native CAD platform offering.

REST APIs, FeatureScript (custom open source programming language), and Onshape App Store integrations. | SOLIDWORKS API (C#, VB.NET), macros, large third-party add-on market. | Relatively closed ecosystem. CAA C++ API, CATIA V5 macros (VBA). | NX Open API (C++, C#, Python, Java), journaling and toolbar customization. | Fusion API (Python, C++), scripts and add-ins, Autodesk App Store | Inventor API (COM, .NET), powerful "iLogic" for rule-based automation, and Autodesk App Store. |
